title.target: Get on, fall out, make up

objective: Al terminar usas phrasal verbs de relaciones (get on, fall out, make up, split up, look up to, count on) y entiendes su separabilidad.

warmup.prompt_es: Los phrasal verbs son esenciales en inglés cotidiano. Los de relaciones son de los más usados: llevarse bien, pelearse, reconciliarse, romper…

input.text: My sister Laura and I have always got on well, but last year we fell out. We had an argument about money, and for months we didn't speak. I was really upset, because I look up to her. She is the one I count on when I have a problem. In the end, I called her and we made up. She said sorry first, and I told her it didn't matter. Now we get along better than ever. Her boyfriend, however, broke up with her last month. They had been going out for three years. She is still getting over it, but she says she's coming to terms with it. I'm trying to cheer her up. We often go out together, and I always ask her to tell me what's on her mind. Last night we stayed up until two talking and laughing. I think things are looking up.
input.es: Mi hermana Laura y yo siempre nos hemos llevado bien, pero el año pasado nos peleamos. Tuvimos una discusión por dinero y durante meses no nos hablamos. Estaba muy disgustada porque la admiro. Es la persona con la que cuento cuando tengo un problema. Al final la llamé y nos reconciliamos. Ella pidió perdón primero y yo le dije que no importaba. Ahora nos llevamos mejor que nunca. Su novio, sin embargo, rompió con ella el mes pasado. Llevaban tres años saliendo. Todavía lo está superando, pero dice que lo va aceptando. Intento animarla. A menudo salimos juntas y siempre le pido que me cuente qué piensa. Anoche nos quedamos despiertas hasta las dos hablando y riendo. Creo que las cosas están mejorando.

glossary.example: I look up to my sister.
They went out for three years.
She's coming to terms with it.

md_es: **Phrasal verbs de relaciones**
| Phrasal verb | Significado | Ejemplo |
| *get on (well) with* | llevarse bien con | *I get on well with my sister.* |
| *fall out with* | pelearse con | *I fell out with my friend.* |
| *make up (with)* | reconciliarse | *We made up yesterday.* |
| *break up / split up (with)* | romper | *They broke up last month.* |
| *go out with* | salir con (pareja) | *He's going out with Ana.* |
| *look up to* | admirar | *I look up to my teacher.* |
| *look down on* | despreciar | *Don't look down on others.* |
| *count on / rely on* | contar con | *You can count on me.* |
| *get over* | superar | *She got over the flu.* |
| *cheer (someone) up* | animar | *Let's cheer him up.* |
| *let (someone) down* | defraudar | *Don't let me down.* |
| *put up with* | aguantar | *I can't put up with the noise.* |
**Separables e inseparables**
- **Inseparables** (el complemento va **después**): *get on with, look up to, count on, put up with, get over*.
- ✔ *I look up to her.* · ✘ *I look her up to.*
- **Separables** (el pronombre va **en medio**): *cheer up, let down, make up (inventar)*.
- ✔ *Cheer her up.* · ✔ *Cheer up your friend.* · ✘ *Cheer up her.*
- **Intransitivos** (sin complemento): *We made up. They broke up. Things are looking up.*
**Con -ing después de preposición:** *I'm used to getting up early. I'm looking forward to seeing you.*

**Ojo:** *make up* tiene varios significados: reconciliarse, maquillar(se), inventar. *Break up* también significa 'terminar el curso'. *Fall out* ≠ *fall down*. *Go out with* implica relación; *go out* a secas es 'salir'.
Pronunciación: acento en la **partícula** en muchos phrasal verbs (*get ˈon, fall ˈout, make ˈup*) cuando son intransitivos.
